subject: Location-based Supplement Framework for Remote Offers
messages:
From: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@talentpartners.com>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michaela Jones <m.jones@fastscale.ai>
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: New senior infra candidate — question on location-based pay

Hi Camila,

We have a strong senior infra candidate (FastScale) who is open to joining Redwood remotely. They are currently located in Spain but are considering the option to move to Portugal or remain in Madrid. The hiring manager (Michaela) asked whether Redwood has a standard approach to location differentials or supplements for EU-based remote hires versus US HQ offers.

Quick context: the role would be L5 IC; the recruiter is proposing a base that sits near our US median for L5, but the candidate has asked whether we apply any COLA or location-based allowance that would change the offer.

Could you point me to the current guideline or let me know how to handle in the short term? Attaching the candidate packet for context.

Thanks — and happy to jump on a short sync if easier.

— Olivia
Talent Partners
olivia.hart@talentpartners.com
Attach: candidate-packet-fastscale.pdf (summary)

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, olivia.hart@talentpartners.com
Date: Wed, 16 Jun 2027 10:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New senior infra candidate — question on location-based pay

Hi all — looping you in.

Short ask: we need a consistent, defensible way to handle remote hires who are physically in EU/APAC vs US hires so offers are timely and compliant. Current situation (informal):
- For US remote hires we typically align to US bands with limited locality adjustments.
- For EU/APAC we have been doing ad-hoc supplements (0–10%) based on market and payroll friction.

Proposal (attached: location-supplement-framework-v1.xlsx): create a small set of location supplements (bands by region and city tiers) that are applied as a one-line supplement on offers, rather than changing base bands. This keeps base bands consistent across the company and makes approvals simpler.

Can Laura or Maya advise on feasibility for payroll and comp governance? Vivek — can you flag any cost/approval limits we should bake in (e.g., up to 7% can be approved by hiring manager + finance; >7% needs SVP sign-off)?

If we can agree quickly I want to offer this candidate by next week.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Hiring Manager — Infrastructure
Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, olivia.hart@talentpartners.com
Date: Thu, 17 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New senior infra candidate — question on location-based pay

Thanks for the context, Camila. I looked at comps for L5 across US/EU/APAC and sketched a short framework (attached: comp-band-summary-2027.pdf). Key points:

- Base bands remain global by level.
- Introduce a location supplement table: Tier 1 (high-cost cities) +8–12%, Tier 2 +3–7%, Tier 3 0–2%. EU markets we typically fall into Tier 2 for Madrid/Portugal; large metro Western EU (London, Paris) Tier 1. APAC varies heavily.
- Supplements should be additive and visible as a line on the offer, with a fixed review cadence.
- For roles tied to regulatory payroll (local entity hires) check local statutory costs — these are separate and must be included.

Questions:
1) Should supplements be capped as a dollar amount or a percent? I prefer percent to keep consistency across bands.
2) Do we want manager-level approval thresholds (e.g., up to 5% manager + People Ops; 5–10% Head of Hiring + Finance; >10% People Leadership + CFO)?

I flagged some sample ranges in the attachment and highlighted Madrid/Portugal as +4% in the model. Happy to refine.

— Laura
Compensation Partner
Redwood Inference
Attach: comp-band-summary-2027.pdf

From: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, olivia.hart@talentpartners.com
Date: Fri, 18 Jun 2027 11:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New senior infra candidate — question on location-based pay

Agree with the approach. A few operational constraints from finance:

- We should default to percent-based supplements (cleaner across bands).
- Approval matrix recommendation:
  • Up to 6%: Hiring manager + People Ops (auto-approve in Workday/offer tool)
  • 6–12%: Hiring manager + Head of Product/Platform + Finance (manual review)
  • >12%: Requires ELT approval (VP/CFO sign-off)

- Cost modeling note: applying a 4% supplement to L5 hires across the open requisitions (estimate 12 hires) increases run-rate ~0.6% of payroll — acceptable within current hiring plan budget but we need monthly tracking.
- Payroll/benefits: if candidate moves to a local contract in EU, statutory employer costs may exceed supplements; People Ops must coordinate with Legal.

For the current candidate: if we treat Spain/Portugal as +4% supplement we can offer within the manager threshold.

— Vivek
Head of Finance, Redwood Inference

From: maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>
To: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, olivia.hart@talentpartners.com
Date: Sun, 20 Jun 2027 16:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: New senior infra candidate — question on location-based pay

Thanks — operational notes from Hiring Ops:

- Offer language: include a "Location Supplement" line in the compensation section with percentage and duration (recommended initial 12 months, then review).
- Payroll: for remote EU hires we strongly prefer to onboard on the local entity where possible; if not, supplement is fine but must include an explicit statement that statutory employer costs are separate.
- Immigration/tax: candidate must confirm tax residency at offer acceptance — we also need to run a quick payroll feasibility check for Portugal in case they relocate.
- Offer timeline: once comp is approved I can prepare the offer letter within 24–48 hours.

Candidate note: Olivia, confirm whether candidate expects exact US-equivalent total comp or is flexible. If they seek parity, we should be transparent about the supplement approach.

— Maya
Head of Hiring Operations
Redwood Inference

From: camila_reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Hart <olivia.hart@talentpartners.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, maya_srinivasan <maya_srinivasan@redwood.ai>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2027 18:03:00 -0700
Subject: Final: Location Supplement approved for FastScale candidate (L5)

Hi Olivia —

Thanks for the patience. Per the team discussion above, we will proceed as follows for the FastScale senior infra candidate:

- Offer: base aligned to L5 global band + Location Supplement of 4% (applied as a separate line item, duration 12 months)
- Approvals: within hiring manager threshold; finance has signed off on the supplement level and monthly tracking will be added to the hiring dashboard.
- Next steps for you: confirm candidate's preferred payroll jurisdiction (Spain vs Portugal) and whether they expect a US-equivalent headline comp. Once confirmed, Maya will prepare the offer letter.

Olivia — please treat this as the approved framework for similar Western EU remote hires unless otherwise noted. Laura and Maya — please add the finalized supplement table to Comp central and share the link. I've attached the working spreadsheet we used.

Thanks everyone for the quick turnaround.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Hiring Manager — Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
Attach: location-supplement-framework-v1.xlsx
